title: Almine Rech Shanghai stages Tom Wesselmann's mainland China solo debut
summary: Almine Rech Shanghai is presenting Tom Wesselmann’s first solo exhibition in mainland China, on view from November 9, 2026 to January 9, 2027. "The Greatness of the Everyday", Tom Wesselmann’s first solo exhibition in mainland China, offers an opportunity to discover or revisit the work of this major figure in American Pop Art. The exhibition traces the development of his practice through the series that defined it, from his early Great American Nudes to his late Sunset Nudes. Wesselmann worked tirelessly, developing distinct series linked by recurring subjects and evolving aesthetic interests. Driven by a desire to innovate, he explored new media and approaches to composition through familiar motifs. His experiments included collage, unconventional cropping, and dramatic shifts in scale. title: George Eastman Museum presents 'GAG,' a new framework for 21st-century photography and video
summary: The George Eastman Museum presents GAG, an exhibition that proposes a bold new framework for understanding twenty-first-century photography and video. What is “gag”? Both noun and verb, gag provokes strong feelings. Beginning with the cinematic sight gag and its long history of comic interruption, the exhibition expands to put in play uses of the terms associated with queer ballroom vernacular, judicial gag orders, BDSM and kink, choking and retching, and the dark feedback loops of social media and meme culture. What emerges is a rich conceptual language for work that refuses easy categorization: violent and slapstick, icky and sublime, funny and anxious, all at once. “The George Eastman Museum has a long history of groundbreaking exhibitions that highlight major artistic developments,” said

title: Florence's Accademia Gallery receives rare Alinari collection documenting five centuries of Italian drawing
summary: The Galleria dell'Accademia di Firenze has received a major donation of 26 volumes from the Biblioteca di Disegni (Library of Drawings), a remarkable publishing project produced by the historic Italian photographic firm Fratelli Alinari. The collection, donated by Claudio de Polo-Saibanti, contains more than 1,040 reproductions of drawings by leading Italian masters dating from the 14th to the 18th centuries. The donation will be presented at the Galleria dell'Accademia on Monday, November 23, 2026, at 6 p.m., during an event bringing together museum officials and specialists in art and photographic history. title: Christopher Le Brun explores color, memory, and inward terrain in new Lisson show
summary: Lisson opened an exhibition of new work by Christopher Le Brun, presenting an extensive sequence of canvases informed by a lifetime’s thinking about painting. The exhibition reaps the rewards of Le Brun’s experience, expressing his mastery of colour and touch while continuing his exploration into the fundamental characteristics of painting: surface and depth, tone and light, memory and imagination. Titled The Mind’s Weather, the exhibition highlights the vital role that changeability, or openness to change, plays in Le Brun’s paintings. In the accompanying essay by Barry Phipps, the art historian describes this group of paintings as “a series of propositions, each testing that resistance from different viewpoints through the time of the works.” “Since the invention of perspective, the task of the background has been to disappear into context and allow the subject to take the foreground; the landscape carries a rider, a sky stands behind a tower. title: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao presents an immersive site-specific installation by Zadie Xa
summary: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is presenting in situ: Zadie Xa. Seed Pattern, the fourth chapter of the Museum’s “in situ” series, a program that invites artists to create site-specific works in dialogue with the gallery’s architecture. Conceived as a platform for ambitious projects by leading contemporary artists, in situ highlights practices that expand the possibilities of sculpture, installation, and multimedia. Each presentation engages directly with the Museum’s distinctive gallery dedicated to the series, transforming it into environments where architecture and artistic imagination converge. Zadie Xa has developed an expansive practice that addresses the nature of diasporic identities, global histories, familial legacies and interspecies communication. She explores these themes through immersive installations that appeal to the sensory experience of the viewer, often incorporating painting, sculpture, textile, sound and performance elements. title: Marilyn Monroe's final photo sessions take center stage in Paris auction of Bert Stern's personal archive
summary: A remarkable collection of photographs from the personal archive of American photographer Bert Stern (1929–2013), including images from his legendary final sessions with Marilyn Monroe, will go under the hammer at Gros & Delettrez in Paris on December 2, 2026. Organized in collaboration with the Bert Stern Trust and the agencies Artsphere and H&K, the sale will feature approximately 150 lots, offering collectors a rare opportunity to acquire prints that the photographer kept in his own collection. The auction comes during the centenary year of Monroe's birth on June 1, 1926, and marks the first time the Bert Stern Trust has released photographs from the artist's personal holdings. Among the highlights are vintage prints, contact sheets, and works produced by Stern himself, some bearing handwritten annotations that provide an unusually intimate glimpse into his creative process. title: Nan Goldin to debut major new work at the Southbank Centre's Hayward Gallery
summary: The Hayward Gallery will open its major solo exhibition by acclaimed American artist and activist Nan Goldin, rounding off the Southbank Centre’s 75th anniversary year. Marking Goldin’s first institutional show in the UK since 2002, the presentation will debut a new film alongside other recent moving image works and photographs, offering a rare insight into how we can survive, empathise and find beauty in uncertain times. Over the past five decades, Goldin has documented personal relationships, addiction and queer communities. Her unflinching images transformed photography by closing the distance between the observer and the observed, capturing the rawness of her own life. Comprising deeply intimate photographs and slideshows, her stories embrace the complexity of life as universal tales of love and loss. title: Rare Sikh Empire palace faâade estimated at €60,000-€80,000 to headline Paris auction
summary: A monumental carved wooden palace façade from the Sikh Empire, dating to approximately 1800–1850, will be among the highlights of Gros & Delettrez's Arts of Islam and India auction in Paris on December 4, 2026. Measuring 3.14 meters high and more than five meters wide, the architectural ensemble is attributed to craftsmen from Bhera, in the Punjab region, and carries an estimate of €60,000–€80,000. Carved from Himalayan cedar, the façade is the centerpiece of a collection assembled by a former textile industrialist from Lyon, who acquired the work in Villeurbanne in 1989. The collection, which includes 29 lots in the upcoming sale, reflects the owner's longstanding interest in the artistic traditions of the Indian subcontinent, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. title: M Leuven presents Nefeli Papadimouli's first solo exhibition in Belgium
summary: M has followed Nefeli Papadimouli’s work for several years, first collaborating with her during the Playground festival in 2021. Five years later, the artist returns with ‘ANAMESA’, her first solo exhibition in Belgium. At M, Papadimouli is showing recent works in various media alongside new textile sculptures. She has also created a new performance especially for the exhibition. With a background in architecture and visual art, Nefeli Papadimouli (b. 1988, Athens; lives and works in Paris) has developed a multifaceted practice that brings together sculpture, installation, textiles, video and performance. Inspired by phenomenology, feminism and contemporary political theory, she explores how distance, proximity and movement shape processes of coexistence, conflict, negotiation and interdependence. title: Meet Mary: New display at Kensington Palace to tell the story of history's forgotten Queen
summary: She’s the Queen that history forgot; a young woman who ascended her deposed father’s throne and changed the rules of the monarchy forever. Meet Mary. In March 2027 the Queen’s State Apartments built by Queen Mary II will reopen with a new display about the Stuart monarch who, with her husband and joint ruler William III, built Kensington Palace and made it her home. Her story will be brought to life with rare surviving items, united in the rooms where she lived – and died – as a Sovereign Queen. The newly restored and presented rooms at Kensington Palace will feature new research and rarely seen treasures from public and private collections across Britain and Europe that reveal the woman behind the Crown. Mary II was joint Sovereign of England, Scotland and Ireland in the late 17th century, and a powerful political mover in her own right. title: Hayward Gallery opens first UK solo exhibition of Armenian-Lithuanian artist Andrius Arutiunian
summary: The Hayward Gallery, in partnership with the RC Foundation, Taiwan (R.O.C.), will present Andrius Arutiunian: They Tried to Count Us. This will mark the Armenian-Lithuanian artist and composer’s first solo exhibition in the UK and the eighth exhibition in the RC Foundation Project Space Exhibition Series, which showcases the next generation of emerging international artists. Andrius Arutiunian: They Tried to Count Us takes place in the HENI Project Space in the Southbank Centre’s Hayward Gallery – a space that offers the opportunity for audiences to discover exhibitions from new artistic voices for free. Bringing together new commissions and recent work, They Tried to Count Us taps into humanity’s continuous quest to define the afterlife. The exhibition will expand the artist’s ongoing investigation into representations of the underworld and cosmos across time and cultures. title: Hamiltons presents a previously unseen selection of botanical photographs by Charles Jones
summary: Hamiltons will exhibit a new selection of exceptional works by Charles Jones, previously unseen, at 13 Carlos Place from the 25th of November 2026. In 1998 Hamiltons Gallery presented the first ever exhibition of photographs by Charles Jones, coinciding with the publication of The Plant Kingdom of Charles Hones by Thames & Hudson. In the nearly thirty years, since the works have been widely exhibited, including at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, the Musée de l'Elysée in Lausanne, the Dulwich Picture Gallery in London and the Konstmuseet Gothenburg. Little is known about the life of Charles Jones, aside from the fact he was born in Wolverhampton in 1866 and was employed as a professional gardener at many notable private estates across England. Even less was known about his photographic oeuvre until it was rediscovered by historian and photographic collector Sean Sexton.

title: Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst presents its 2027 programme
summary: For its 2027 exhibition program, the Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst explores the power and politics of storytelling under the overarching theme The stories we carry – Collecting, passing on, telling. Running from February 2027 through January 2028, the year-long lineup spans solo presentations by Mounira Al Solh, Marc Camille Chaimowicz, and Sammy Baloji, alongside an interactive collection showcase and a joint exhibition featuring Colectivo Los Ingrávidos and Riar Rizaldi. Together, these exhibitions examine how personal memories, colonial histories, and alternative cosmologies are preserved, fragmented, and reimagined across generations.The exhibition is an initiative of Bonnefanten, Maastricht, and is organised in collaboration with Arnolfini, Bristol, and Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst, Zurich, in association with Sharjah Art Foundation. summary: The highlight of the auction is a fashion shot by Helmut Newton showing two women in an elegant interior. One is tying the other's eyes closed in preparation for an erotic game or, as the title suggests, a 'Parlour Game' (lot 750, € 25/30,000). Another international superstar among fashion photographers is Peter Lindbergh, from whom there is an iconic image of 'Kate Moss' in a casual pose with a cigarette (lot 752, € 12/15,000). Horst is the master photographer of elegant poses, represented by three exquisite platinum-palladium prints (lots 733-735, from € 4/5,000 to € 5/6,000). title: PICA unveils 2027 program focusing on participation, perception and possibility
summary: The Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts (PICA) presents its 2027 artistic program, bringing together Australian and international artists across four seasons of major commissions, ambitious exhibitions, experimental works and immersive experiences that challenge perspectives and create new opportunities for cultural exchange. Season 1 (5 February – 28 March 2027) at PICA asks: when visibility is challenged, what becomes possible? Presented in association with Perth Festival, the season brings together local, national and international voices to examine the politics of visibility. Through exhibitions and new commissions, artists explore who and what is seen, how surveillance shapes representation, and how we can experience the world beyond sight. title: Nottingham Contemporary presents its 2027-28 exhibitions programme
summary: Nottingham Contemporary has unveiled its exhibition programme for 2027–28, bringing together six major presentations exploring Indigenous identity, political resistance, cultural memory, and the relationship between art and social change. The programme will feature a series of institutional firsts, including exhibitions dedicated to Guatemalan painter Francisco Tún, Sámi artist and architect Joar Nango, Iranian-Aotearoan artist Selina Ershadi, Croatian textile pioneer Jagoda Buić, and Angolan artist Sandra Poulson. Running from February 2027 through January 2028, the programme will also present a collaborative exhibition examining the role of artistic production in the Philippines' national democratic movement. title: Nantucket Historical Association to open Basket Museum
summary: The Nantucket Historical Association announced the opening of the Basket Museum, a new museum dedicated to the island's iconic tradition of basket making. The museum will open to the public in the summer of 2027 at the historic Macy Warehouse, 12 Straight Wharf — one of Nantucket's most prominent harborside landmarks. Construction of the new museum space begins this January. The NHA also announces that the museum's main gallery will be named The Connie Anne and Jeremiah Harris Gallery, in recognition of the Harris family's transformative lead gift in support of the project. “As passionate basket collectors, we could not be more thrilled to be supporting this new museum for the island community and visitors alike. title: Qatar Museums launches Rubaiya Qatar, its major new contemporary arts quadrennial
summary: Qatar Museums (QM) today marked the public opening of the inaugural edition of Rubaiya Qatar, QM's international contemporary arts quadrennial, running through 30 April 2027. Established under the leadership of Her Excellency Sheikha Al Mayassa bint Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Chairperson of Qatar Museums, and developed and organised under ALRIWAQ Arts + Architecture—Rubaiya Qatar’s institutional home and principal venue—the quadrennial reinforces Qatar’s role as a dynamic cultural hub for artistic experimentation, empowering new generations of artists and thinkers. title: US Mint: Rarest coins of 21st century to be auctioned
summary: Stack’s Bowers Galleries has been selected by the United States Mint to auction limited edition July 4th Privy Mark 2.5-Ounce Silver Quarters celebrating the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence and America’s founding. Produced during a special ceremony at the Philadelphia Mint on July 4, 2026, only 250 of these silver quarters were struck for sale to the public, and they will be available exclusively through the Stack’s Bowers Galleries auction on Tuesday, December 1, 2026, at 3 p.m. EST (12 p.m. PST). Struck in 2.5 ounces of .999 fine silver with a bespoke matte finish and the striking sequence laser engraved on the edge, they celebrate America’s 250 year journey with a tangible treasure that is both symbolically and physically mesmerizing. title: Chillida Leku opens a dialogue between Gonzalo and Eduardo Chillida's painting and sculpture
summary: Chillida Leku has opened Peering out toward the Horizon. The Chillida Brothers, Eduardo and Gonzalo at Zabalaga, the first exhibition dedicated to the two brothers, bringing together Gonzalo’s painting and Eduardo’s sculpture in a dialogue between their artistic practices. On view at Zabalaga farmhouse until 7 March 2027, the exhibition brings their creative worlds together for the first time, exploring the affinities and distinctive characteristics of their respective artistic languages. Curated by Alicia Chillida and initiated by the heirs of both artists, the exhibition brings together more than 100 works by Gonzalo Chillida and a selection of over 30 works by Eduardo Chillida from the museum’s collection. title: Hauser & Wirth announces reprsentation of artist Ser Serpas
summary: Hauser & Wirth announced its worldwide representation of Los Angeles-born artist Ser Serpas, in collaboration with LC Queisser of Tbilisi and Cologne. Born in 1995, Serpas currently lives and works in Paris but regularly moves between such cities as New York, Los Angeles, Geneva and Tbilisi. Over the past decade she has attracted international attention for a restless, multifaceted oeuvre in constant transformation, moving between sculpture, painting, video, poetry, photography and performance in a complex, provocative amalgam. Her exhibitions are staged encounters in which found objects, paintings and live events merge and expand like scenes in a film. title: mk2 museum in Paris, France, will open in March 2027 with Jean Jullien's exhibition "The Republic"
summary: Opening in March 2027, mk2 museum will take shape within mk2 bibliothèque, introducing a new 1,500 sq m space dedicated to exhibition-making and creative exploration.Spanning cinema, visual arts, music and video games, the museum will explore the creative disciplines shaping contemporary culture and the way it is experienced today. Open seven days a week, 365 days a year, from morning until midnight, it will offer visitors the chance to experience its exhibitions throughout the day and late into the night. For over 50 years, mk2 has stood for a more independent vision of cinema, one that puts artists and creative freedom first, and with mk2 museum, that vision takes on a new dimension. Conceived as a space for experimentation and discovery, the museum will give artists room to explore new creative territories, while opening up fresh ways for audiences

title: Gallery Wendi Norris announces exclusive representation of interdisciplinary artist Selva Aparicio
summary: Gallery Wendi Norris announced the exclusive representation of interdisciplinary artist Selva Aparicio (b. 1987, Barcelona, Spain; based in Alfred, NY). This announcement follows Aparicio’s 2025–26 solo presentation, What Remains, at Gallery Wendi Norris and comes ahead of her solo exhibition, De tot Cor (With All My Heart), which opens at Pioneer Works in Brooklyn, NY, on January 17, 2027. Working in sculpture and installation, Aparicio uses slow, labor-intensive processes to address memory, loss, and care. She gathers materials that are usually overlooked or thrown away, such as cemetery flowers, cicada wings, and human hair, and transforms them into objects that carry personal and collective histories. title: Peh Family's impossibly rare 1894 Hupeh Dollar at Heritage HKINF World & Ancient Coins Auction
summary: One of the most coveted treasures in all of Chinese numismatics will make a rare appearance to the collecting community when it is offered in Heritage’s HKINF World & Ancient Coins Platinum Session and Signature® Auction – Hong Kong Dec. 5–8. “Rarely do we see this amount, depth and variety of exceptional coins in a single event,” says Kyle Johnson, Heritage’s Managing Director of World & Ancient Coins. “This auction should interest people from all collecting segments of Southeast Asia, and represents Heritage’s status as the premier auction destination for collectors of the region and around the world.” The Hupeh.
